data.title: System Information Discovery
data.summary: The sample queries OS version, architecture, locale, installed hotfixes and hardware details early in execution, typically to select a compatible code path or to decide whether to proceed at all.
data.description:
This is usually the first thing a sample does after any anti-analysis checks, because
everything downstream — which injection technique to use, which persistence mechanism is
available, whether a given exploit applies — depends on it. Some families also use the
results defensively: a locale check that avoids certain countries, or a patch-level check
that withholds an exploit the target is not actually vulnerable to, to limit exposure of
the exploit to telemetry.
data.recommendation:
* Note which system properties were queried; a locale or geofencing check narrows the likely intended target set meaningfully.
* Correlate discovery queries with the capability branches that follow them to understand which code paths this specific host triggered.
* Treat this as routine rather than alarming on its own — it is near-universal — but weight it heavily when it precedes a capability selection branch.
data.short_recommendation: Correlate discovery queries with the capability branches that follow to understand which code paths this host triggered.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Queried OS version, system locale and installed hotfix list, and branched to a 32-bit or 64-bit payload accordingly.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Queried system locale and excluded execution for a short list of configured country codes.
